samples.question: This picture shows one square panel with a dark border. Inside the border is a seven-row, seven-column field of equal square cells; each cell is either dark or pale, and exactly thirteen cells are dark in every picture. Just to the left of the panel, separated from it and from one another by background, float seven dark tally bars, one beside each panel row and vertically centred on that row. The seven bars all have different lengths. A few small clutter marks - little squares, diamonds and narrow upright rules - lie elsewhere on the background, never beside the panel rows, and carry no evidence. Carry out this operation. Keeping each panel row's seven cells together and in their left-to-right order, reorder the seven rows by the length of the bar beside them: the row whose bar is shortest becomes the top row, the row whose bar is next shortest becomes the second row, and so on down to the row with the longest bar, which becomes the bottom row. The rows are never moved sideways and no cell changes colour. The reordered dark cells always form exactly one of six symbols on the seven-by-seven field. 'cross' is a full centre row crossing a full centre column. 'tee' is a full top row with a full centre column hanging from it. 'zigzag' is a flat bar near the top and a flat bar lower down, joined by a short diagonal that runs from the upper bar down and to the left. 'corners' is four separated two-by-two-style corner elbows, one in each corner, with a single dark cell at the centre. 'stripes' is three separated flat bars, one above another, with two empty rows between neighbouring bars. 'columns' is three separated upright bars of equal height with a single dark cell below the middle one. The symbol is never drawn in the picture as it stands: the panel alone shows the seven rows in a scrambled order and settles nothing, and the bars alone give only an order and carry no cell of the symbol, so the panel and the separated gutter must both be read. Which symbol do the reordered dark cells form? Answer with exactly one of: columns, corners, cross, stripes, tee, zigzag.
